source.title: Autoclip: Adaptive Gradient Clipping for Source Separation Networks
source.authors: Prem Seetharaman; G. Wichern; Bryan Pardo; Jonathan Le Roux

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the paper through its references.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies adaptive gradient clipping and measures test performance and training dynamics, but does not test the specific comparisons named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The AutoClip results bear on test performance and a trained network's local smoothness, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gap, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study tests adaptive gradient clipping for speech separation, not any of V1–V8. Adam is held fixed, and local gradient Lipschitz smoothness is neither magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness nor its association with the train-test gap. The discussion invokes smoother minima and cites a V5 original, but reports no batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AutoClip replaces a manually chosen absolute clipping threshold, transfers across differently scaled losses, improves test performance in the tested speech-separation networks, and stabilizes optimization. A percentile hyperparameter remains; applicability to other tasks is proposed as future work.
record.recipe_differences: Tests adaptive gradient clipping with Adam on audio source separation networks; the claim versions concern other interventions and comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Test SI-SDR varies with AutoClip percentile and loss function; no clipping performs worse across the five losses, with a nearly 2 dB drop for LMI and LSNR as described by the authors.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five losses, AutoClip improves speech-separation test SI-SDR over no clipping. At p=10, gains are 0.6, 0.2, 1.7, 0.4, and 2.1 dB for LDC, LWKM, LMI, LMI+WKM, and LSNR respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive gradient clipping can improve held-out speech-separation performance with Adam across loss functions of different scales.

fits_no_version.finding: The smaller network has lower training loss and test SI-SDR of 9.2 versus 8.1 dB with AutoClip. Gradient-norm/local-smoothness correlation is 0.86 versus 0.62.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AutoClip can improve optimization and test performance while changing the relationship between gradient norm and local smoothness along training.

record.peer_reviewed: International Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing
record.problems: The results use one speech separation dataset and the measured performance is SI-SDR rather than a train-test error gap. The smaller-network dynamics comparison is one network configuration; uncertainty estimates are not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond that needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, dataset-size dependence, underfitting, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match the supplied text. These rows belong under fits_no_version rather than evidence for V1–V8. Their cannot_determine states concern applicability to those versions, not whether AutoClip improved measured performance. The shared random seed and absence of reported uncertainty limit assessment of variability.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons and their relation to the train-test gap.
